title: n435vr
Karbala
hook: There was no pledge of allegiance to Yazid. The water was cut off. On the tenth of Muharram, the Ahl al-Bayt were martyred.
scenes.0.text: When Mu'awiya died, rule passed to **Yazid**. The governor of Medina, al-Walid, summoned **Imam Husayn** and asked him to pledge allegiance to the new rule. A pledge (bay'a) meant giving a word of allegiance. Imam Husayn did not give this word. The decision he made in Medina became the first step of the road he would take with his family.
scenes.0.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 1f4krkm
Yazid
scenes.0.art.actors.2.label: s3kj9h
al-Walid
scenes.1.text: At night the streets of Medina were silent. **Imam Husayn** gathered his family. **Lady Zaynab** was beside him, the children were asleep. Before setting out he stopped by his grandfather's grave. He bent to the earth and stayed there a long time. In the morning the caravan would take the road to Mecca.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: 135phaa
Zaynab
scenes.2.text: In Mecca there was the umra. Letters came one after another from Kufa. "Come. We have no governor. We will pledge allegiance to you." **Imam Husayn** did not immediately send an army. He sent his cousin **Muslim b. Aqil** ahead. Muslim entered Kufa. The houses filled. Thousands of hands were raised in allegiance. For a few days the city breathed with him. Imam Husayn waited for news in Mecca. The invitation was crowded on paper. The letters multiplied.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 869gah
Muslim
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.3.text: In Kufa the wind turned. **Yazid**'s governor Ubaydullah b. Ziyad entered the city. The doors closed. Those who had pledged allegiance the day before hid in their homes. **Muslim b. Aqil** was left alone in the streets. He was captured. He was brought to the gallows. He was martyred. His head was sent to **Yazid**. The news reached the caravan late. **Imam Husayn** had already turned back toward the road to Kufa. The invitation had turned into a trap. The journey did not stop.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 869gah
Muslim
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: 165bwyt
Ibn Ziyad
scenes.4.text: The gate of the palace was shadowed. **Muslim b. Aqil** had been captured. He asked for cold water. Muslim b. Amr did not give a single drop. The reported reply was that he could not drink until he had tasted the fire of hell. Then Amr b. Hurayth had water brought. Muslim raised the bowl to his mouth. The wound in his mouth prevented him from drinking the water. He could not drink. This thirst recalls the thirst of his uncle's son **Imam Husayn** at Karbala. It is not told that he called out to the people for water during the battle.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 869gah
Muslim
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: 1xk8ua9
Amr b. Hurayth
scenes.5.text: In the noon heat of the desert, **al-Hurr b. Yazid** and his horsemen blocked the caravan's way. The soldiers and the horses were thirsty. **Imam Husayn** had the water-skins opened. He gave water to the force that had come to stop him, and to their horses. Then he reminded them of the letters of invitation that had come from Kufa. Al-Hurr had not yet drawn his sword. The two forces traveled on in the same dust.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: ij42up
al-Hurr
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.6.text: It was the 2nd of Muharram. The horses halted on a plain. **Imam Husayn** asked the name of the place. "Karbala," they said. Karbala is the desert of karb and bala. Karb is grief. Bala is a heavy trial. The Prophet had announced to Imam Husayn in advance the name of the place where he would be martyred in just this way. Gabriel had brought a handful of earth from Karbala and entrusted it to **Umm Salama**. He had said, "When this earth turns to blood, Imam Husayn will have been martyred." When Imam Husayn heard the name he said: "This is the place of karb and bala. Dismount. Here our blood will be shed." Then he bought this land. From the people of Nineveh and al-Ghadiriyya he bought a place about four miles wide and four miles long for 60,000 dirhams. Then he gave the same land back to them as charity. The condition was this: they would show the way to those who came to visit his grave and would host them for three days. The tents were pitched. **Umar b. Sa'd** came with an army on behalf of **Yazid**'s governor. He wanted the governorship of Rayy. In return he had been ordered to march against Imam Husayn. The plain turned into a military camp. The caravan was small. The opposite slope was crowded.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: 17b9rtg
Umar b. Sa'd
scenes.7.text: On the 7th of Muharram the Euphrates was cut off. Martyrdom was three days away. The water flowed beside the tent. Drinking was forbidden. The prohibition came down from **Yazid**'s order in Kufa. The children opened their mouths. The women fell silent. **Imam Husayn** too was thirsty. The household still kept its dignity. The clothes were clean. The postures were composed. The sultanate that **Mu'awiya** had founded begrudged even a sip of water to the grandson's children. The night wind carried dust. In the morning there was thirst again.
scenes.7.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: 135phaa
Zaynab
scenes.8.text: At night it was hot inside the tent. The children looked for something to moisten their lips. The women lowered their voices. **Imam Husayn** too was thirsty. The clothes were still in order. The back was not yet broken. The Euphrates was near. Drinking was forbidden. The prohibition came down from **Yazid**'s order in Kufa. In the morning the same thirst was there again. This was the weight of three days.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.8.art.actors.1.label: 1xxr12u
Lady Zaynab
scenes.9.text: It was the evening of the 9th of Muharram. Thursday. One day before Ashura. **Shimr b. Dhi al-Jawshan** came before the caravan. It is reported that he called them "the sons of my sister." This is described as the same maternal lineage. It is not said that he was their own maternal uncle. Their mother was **Umm al-Banin**. Aman is a word of safe-conduct for life. Shimr spoke on behalf of **Yazid**. "Do not die with Imam Husayn." The young men answered: "May God curse you and your safe-conduct. When there is no safe-conduct for the son of the Messenger of God, is there safe-conduct for us?" **Abbas** put it plainly: "May your hands wither. Are we to leave our brother Imam Husayn and enter the obedience of the accursed?" He tore up the paper of safe-conduct. He threw it away. In the tent **Imam Zayn al-Abidin** was ill. **Lady Zaynab** was waiting at his side.
scenes.9.art.actors.0.label: 10ec1dz
Shimr
scenes.9.art.actors.1.label: 17aitug
Abbas
scenes.9.art.actors.2.label: 135phaa
Zaynab
scenes.10.text: The front of the tents was dust. **Lady Zaynab** was with the children. She was not ill. She kept the little ones at the hem of her skirt. She tried to keep fear away from them. The one who was ill was **Imam Zayn al-Abidin**. He was inside the tent.
scenes.10.art.actors.0.label: 1xxr12u
Lady Zaynab
scenes.10.art.actors.1.label: ms2fd7
Imam Zayn al-Abidin
scenes.11.text: The one who was ill was **Imam Zayn al-Abidin**. For this reason he could not go out to battle. There were those who wanted to kill him. There were also those who said, "This illness is enough for him." **Lady Zaynab** was not ill. In captivity she was taken to Kufa and Damascus with this illness (of his) beside her.
scenes.11.art.actors.0.label: ms2fd7
Imam Zayn al-Abidin
scenes.11.art.actors.1.label: 1xxr12u
Lady Zaynab
scenes.12.text: It was the night of the 9th of Muharram. **Umar b. Sa'd** gave a respite until morning. **Imam Husayn** gathered his friends and those who had joined along the way. The wick of the tent burned low. He lifted his pledge of allegiance from them. "Use the night, use its darkness, like a camel. Go. You do not have to stay with me. Yazid wants me." Some truly took advantage of the darkness and left him. The bedouins who had joined on the road hoping for spoils had mostly dispersed, especially when it was heard that Kufa had fallen and **Muslim b. Aqil** had been martyred. Only a small number of loyal people remained. Those who stayed gave their word. **Abbas** said: "Even if I were killed and brought back to life a thousand times, I would still not leave you." **Muslim b. Awsaja** said the same. **Zuhayr** too: "Even if I were killed and brought back to life a thousand times, I would still not leave you." The night was filled with worship. The Qur'an was recited. Swords stayed in their sheaths, foreheads touched the ground in prostration. This loyalty met the morning.
scenes.12.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.13.text: On the morning of the tenth of Muharram the sun rose red. **Imam Husayn** mounted his horse and came out before the opposing army. “Do you not know me? I am the grandson of the Messenger of God. My father is Imam Ali, my mother is Lady Fatima.” In the opposing ranks some lowered their heads. When his speech was over, the archers began to prepare.
scenes.13.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.14.text: When the sermon ended, they came to the front of the tent. **Lady Zaynab** was beside the door. A child clung to her skirt. **Imam Husayn** looked at them. This was the last look of farewell. The morning was the morning on which the household would be scattered.
scenes.14.art.actors.0.label: 1xxr12u
Lady Zaynab
scenes.14.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.15.text: On the morning of Ashura, **al-Hurr** trembled. He pulled his horse's reins. "I am between Paradise and the fire," he said. He spurred his horse. He came to **Imam Husayn**. He dismounted. "It was I who held you on the road." Imam Husayn forgave him. He changed sides. He fought in the first rank. He was martyred the same morning. Imam Husayn stood at his head. "You are free (hurr), and your mother bore you free." This repentance was a conscience that broke away from **Yazid**'s army. The plain saw its first blood from this turn.
scenes.15.art.actors.0.label: ij42up
al-Hurr
scenes.15.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.16.text: Then the companions came out one by one. **Habib b. Muzahir** was an old friend of **Imam Ali**. His hair had turned white. He fought in the field like a young man. **Zuhayr b. Qayn** had returned from the pilgrimage road and joined the caravan. His sword did not come down until it fell. According to the report, **Wahb** also came out. His mother sent him back. "My son, stand before the grandson of the Prophet." Wahb returned. He was martyred. Each of them went by his own name. The front of the tent grew a little quieter with each return.
scenes.16.art.actors.0.label: 12xovx4
Habib
scenes.16.art.actors.1.label: 1qy9wc7
Zuhayr
scenes.16.art.actors.2.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.17.text: At Ashura noon, **Abu Thumama** reminded him of the prayer time. **Imam Husayn** looked at the sky and asked that they wait until the prayer was over. The opposing ranks did not wait. As the archers drew their bows, **Zuhayr** and **Sa'id b. Abdullah** stepped in front of those praying. Sa'id did not leave his place. The prayer was completed under the arrows.
scenes.17.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.17.art.actors.1.label: hm7f2b
Sa'id
scenes.18.text: **Ali al-Akbar** came out into the field. He was **Imam Husayn**'s son. His face resembled the Prophet's. His father looked at him. His eyes filled. "O God, I complain to You about these people. They are killing the young man who most resembles Your Messenger." Ali al-Akbar spurred his horse. There was astonishment in the opposing ranks. Ali al-Akbar was handsome and brave. His sword flashed. Then the arrows caught up. He returned to his father's arms. Imam Husayn laid him on the ground. A cry broke out from the tent. The field fell silent with the name of a son.
scenes.18.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.18.art.actors.1.label: 1ta4mau
Ali al-Akbar
scenes.19.text: The turn came to **Qasim**. He was **Imam Hasan**'s son. He was young. He asked his uncle for permission to go out into the field. **Imam Husayn** hesitated. Then he gave Qasim permission to go to battle. According to the report, Qasim had been asked about death. He had said, "Sweeter than honey." He went out into the field. The small sword in his hand looked large. The opposing army attacked a child. His blessed head was split by a blow from Ibn Fudayl al-Azdi. It is related that he called out to his uncle. Imam Husayn reached him. He pressed him to his chest. He laid his body beside the martyrs of the Hashimites. At the threshold of the tent, one more nephew was missing. Imam Hasan's peace treaty was remembered on this plain with the blood of his son.
scenes.19.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.19.art.actors.1.label: 1wk9ud0
Qasim
scenes.20.text: In the tents the little girls were crying from thirst. **Sakina** was at the front. They were crying, "Water! Uncle, water!" **Abbas** could not bear this cry. He took the water-skin. He tore through the enemy ranks. Fighting blow after blow, he reached the Euphrates. He himself was thirsty. He took the water in his palm. **Imam Husayn** had not drunk while thirsty. He poured the water in his palm back. He wanted to fill the water-skin and return to the tents. He was so handsome and imposing that he was called Qamar Bani Hashim. It means the Moon of the Hashimites. His face was luminous, his stature tall. When he mounted a horse his feet would touch the ground. His strength was described as the firmest arm of Bani Hashim. He was also the one who carried the banner. On the return he fell martyred. The water did not reach the tents. **Imam Husayn** came to his brother's side. "Now my back is broken." The water remained in the hands of **Yazid**'s army again.
scenes.20.art.actors.0.label: 17aitug
Abbas
scenes.20.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.21.text: **Lady Zaynab** brought out the baby who had not seen water for three days. His name was **Ali al-Asghar**. His little face was beautiful. His throat was parched. **Imam Husayn** held him up before the army. "What has this child done to you? Give him a sip of water." The bows were drawn. An arrow of **Harmala** lodged in the throat. The baby bled in his father's palm. Imam Husayn sprinkled the blood on the earth. "When we come into Your presence, be pleased with us." The tent wept.
scenes.21.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.21.art.actors.1.label: 135phaa
Zaynab
scenes.22.text: In the afternoon the field was left to **Imam Husayn**. He was alone. He looked to his right. He looked to his left. "Is there no one to help us?" he called out. The voice struck the tents. His sick son was in bed. The women held him. Imam Husayn drew his sword. He fought heroically. He fought as a single body against an army. He was wounded. He fell. According to the report, his last state was prostration. His forehead on the earth, surrendered to God. **Sinan** thrust a spear. **Khawli** dismounted to cut off the head and trembled. **Shimr** dismounted. He slaughtered him. They cut off his head. The plain fell silent for a moment. The sultanate thought it had defeated an imam in the act of prostration.
scenes.22.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.22.art.actors.1.label: 10ec1dz
Shimr
scenes.23.text: The plain fell silent for a moment. As the dust settled, **Lady Zaynab** was standing before the tents. **Imam Zayn al-Abidin** was still ill. No one was left to return from the field. The tents had not yet been plundered. The next step was captivity.
scenes.23.art.actors.0.label: 1xxr12u
Lady Zaynab
scenes.24.text: **Umar b. Sa'd** shouted. "Who will trample Husayn's chest with his horse?" Ten men came forward. The horses crushed the chest and back. This deed done to the body after death was the army's shame. The dust rose. Blood mixed into the earth. **Yazid**'s victory became the trampling of a place of prostration. From afar the tents saw this.
scenes.24.art.actors.1.label: 17b9rtg
Umar b. Sa'd
scenes.25.text: The tents were entered. The belongings were plundered. Fire was set. The women's veils were pulled off their backs. The little girls' earrings were torn off. The household that had dressed cleanly the day before was stripped on the threshold of captivity. Inside lay **Imam Zayn al-Abidin**. His illness was severe. For this reason he had not been able to come out to the field. "Shall we kill this sick man?" they said. Humayd b. Muslim turned them back. **Lady Zaynab** threw herself over her nephew. She covered him with her own body. Thus Imam Zayn al-Abidin remained alive. Captivity began from this tent.
scenes.25.art.actors.0.label: 135phaa
Zaynab
scenes.25.art.actors.1.label: 1j8dfvq
Sajjad
scenes.26.text: On the same day of Ashura, **Umar b. Sa'd** sent **Imam Husayn**'s head with Khawli and Humayd to **Ibn Ziyad** in Kufa. The heads of the other martyrs also set out. The number was seventy-two. According to the report, the heads were put on spears. They were paraded through the streets of Kufa. The people looked from their windows. The city that had written letters the day before watched the heads today. The road did not end here. Damascus was waiting for **Yazid**.
scenes.26.art.actors.1.label: 165bwyt
Ibn Ziyad
scenes.27.text: The caravan of captives set out on the road to Kufa. Dust covered their feet. **Lady Zaynab** was not ill. She was with the children and the women. **Imam Zayn al-Abidin** was ill. She looked after him. The heads went in front. The city was the city that had written letters the day before. Today the captive household passed before its windows. **Lady Zaynab**'s word was yet to rise in Damascus.
scenes.27.art.actors.0.label: 1xxr12u
Lady Zaynab
scenes.28.text: The windows of Kufa were open. Those who had written letters the day before looked today. It is told that the heads were paraded through the streets. **Lady Zaynab** was with the captives. She was not ill. **Imam Zayn al-Abidin** was ill. The city had fallen silent. Shame was on the face of the one looking from the window. The road did not end here. Damascus stood waiting.
scenes.28.art.actors.1.label: 1xxr12u
Lady Zaynab
scenes.29.text: After Kufa the road turned to Damascus. According to reports, **Lady Zaynab**, the sick **Imam Zayn al-Abidin**, the women and the children were mounted on camels without saddles. There was no saddle. This was not a comfortable journey. It was humiliation. This is how **Yazid**'s sultanate drove the House of the Prophet. Lady Zaynab was beside them. She looked after her sick nephew. The children were also with them. The gate of Damascus would open to this shame.
scenes.29.art.actors.0.label: 1xxr12u
Lady Zaynab
scenes.29.art.actors.1.label: ms2fd7
Imam Zayn al-Abidin
scenes.30.text: As the caravan of captives was taken out on the road to Damascus, two children remained in the dungeon of Kufa. They were the orphans of **Muslim b. Aqil**. Their names were **Muhammad** and **Ibrahim**. The people call them Tiflan-i Muslim, the orphans of Muslim. Their father had come to Kufa to call Imam Husayn, and then had been left alone and martyred. The children stayed in the dungeon for a year. A jailer saw their condition. His heart could not bear it. At night he opened the door and let them go. The two brothers knocked on a woman's door in the dark. The woman took them in, fed them, and put them to bed. Her husband **al-Harith** knew that **Ibn Ziyad** had put a reward on these children. The reward outweighed compassion. At night he took the children and brought them to the bank of the Euphrates. Muhammad and Ibrahim asked permission to pray. Al-Harith stopped. The brothers performed ablution, prayed and embraced each other. The younger one pleaded, "My brother, you endure first, so that I may see you." Al-Harith martyred both. There is no need to prolong the detail. Umayyad tyranny had not ended at Karbala. It had cut down two orphaned children as well. When the news reached **Ibn Ziyad**, even he hesitated. He punished al-Harith. The man who hunted orphans for a reward did not escape his own master's hand.
scenes.30.art.actors.0.label: 1en5zur
Muhammad
scenes.30.art.actors.1.label: 114ijvk
Ibrahim
scenes.30.art.actors.2.label: 1ngjwez
al-Harith
scenes.31.text: The caravan of captives arrived in Damascus. According to reports, **Lady Zaynab**, the sick **Imam Zayn al-Abidin**, the women and the children had come to this gate on camels without saddles. This was a humiliation. **Yazid**'s palace was lit. The head was placed before the assembly. Yazid struck **Imam Husayn**'s lip with a stick. **Lady Zaynab** stood up. She was in chains. Her voice shook the assembly. She threw in Yazid's face him, his lineage and this thing he thought was a victory. "This head in your hand is the head of the grandson of the Prophet." Abu Barza objected. "I saw the Messenger of God kissing this lip." The sultanate was making merry. Zaynab disgraced it. The word lived longer than the sword.
scenes.31.art.actors.0.label: 135phaa
Zaynab
scenes.31.art.actors.1.label: 1f4krkm
Yazid
scenes.32.text: After the assembly, night fell in the ruin of Damascus. **Yazid** had shut the captive household in a ruin. The walls were damp. Inside was **Ruqayya**. She was **Imam Husayn**'s little daughter. She was four years old. She was crying, "Where is my father?" **Lady Zaynab** pressed her to her chest. In her dream she saw her father. When she woke, her cry reached the palace. **Yazid** gave an order. The head was sent on a covered tray. Ruqayya lifted the cover. She saw her father's face. She pressed it to her chest. According to the report, it is related that she died a martyr there from grief.
scenes.32.art.actors.0.label: xhspah
Ruqayya
scenes.32.art.actors.1.label: 135phaa
Zaynab
scenes.33.text: Two years after Karbala, in 63 AH, Medina rose in revolt. **Yazid** gave the army under **Muslim b. Uqba** free rein to plunder the city for three days. This event is called al-Harra. Companions were killed. Horses were tied in the Prophet's Mosque. Women were raped. The people of Medina were forced to pledge allegiance as Yazid's slaves. The Prophet's city was left for three days in the hands of Umayyad tyranny.
scenes.33.art.actors.1.label: 1kuxcv0
Muslim b. Uqba
scenes.34.text: Then the army marched on Mecca. It was 64 AH. The Kaaba was pelted with stones from catapults. The Kaaba's covering and walls burned. **Yazid** died during this siege. After Karbala the sultanate had struck Medina and the Kaaba as well. The tyranny was not considered ended with his death.
scenes.34.art.actors.1.label: 1f4krkm
Yazid
scenes.35.text: The names were not erased. Every year they are remembered at Arbaeen. In 2024 the counter of the shrine of al-Abbas recorded Karbala entries between 1 and 20 Safar as 21,480,525. This is the number of passages through the gate. Each passage does not mean a separate person. The pilgrimage statistic for the same year is 1,833,164 people. The Hajj is not the whole of those who come to the Kaaba throughout the year. Umra was not included in this number. The two counts are separate methods. One is twenty days of entries, the other is the pilgrims of the Hajj season.
scenes.36.text: Yazid took the plain. He could not take the meaning of Islam. Karbala became the day that separated the sultanate from the Prophet's way. The water was cut off. The place of prostration was defiled. Yet the names remained. **Imam Husayn** was remembered every year. **Abbas** was remembered as loyalty. **Ali al-Akbar** was remembered as resemblance. **Lady Zaynab** became the place where the word stood upright. The visit did not let that earth be forgotten. A mourning red as blood kept the truth alive. Karbala did not end. It was told anew in every thirst, in every tyranny.
scenes.36.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
sunni.0.says: Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn are the masters of the youth of Paradise.
sunni.1.says: At Umar b. Sa'd's call, ten men trample Imam Husayn with horses, and his chest and back are crushed. The girls, the sisters and the sick Imam Zayn al-Abidin are taken to Kufa.
sunni.2.says: Yazid has a stick in his hand and strikes Imam Husayn's teeth. Abu Barza objects. The page varies by edition.
sunni.2.grade: The sentence is relayed in history books; on this round, that page of al-Tabari was not separately opened.
sunni.3.says: The cutting off of the water, the killing and the caravan of captives are also told in these histories.
sunni.4.says: On the evening of Thursday the 9th of Muharram, Shimr calls Abbas, Ja'far and Uthman "the sons of my sister" and gives them safe-conduct. The young men say, "May God curse you and your safe-conduct." There is no safe-conduct for the son of the Messenger of God.
sunni.5.says: They pray the noon prayer. Imam Husayn leads the fear prayer. In the afternoon the fighting intensifies and the army reaches him. Al-Hanafi steps forward, arrows rain to the right and left, and he stands until he falls. Zuhayr also fights beside him.
sunni.5.grade: On this page there is no order "shoot them with arrows, let him not pray," nor shield, shoulder or leg.
shia.0.says: Al-Hurr stops the caravan with a thousand horsemen. Imam Husayn gives water to them and their horses.
shia.1.says: On the morning of Ashura al-Hurr chooses Paradise, comes to Imam Husayn and apologizes for having held him on the road.
shia.2.says: Abbas sends forward his brothers of the same mother. They are martyred. Imam Husayn heads for the Euphrates, with Abbas in front of him. The army cuts Abbas off. He fights alone and is killed.
shia.2.grade: The cutting off of the arms, the water-skin and the eye are not on this page. They belong to the maqtal narrative.
shia.3.says: An arrow of Harmala b. al-Kahil lodges in the baby's throat. Zaynab asks for water. In another version the baby has been thirsty for three days and Imam Husayn calls out to the army for a sip of water.
shia.4.says: In the assembly in Damascus Yazid strikes Imam Husayn's teeth with a stick. Zaynab stands up, and her voice resounds through the assembly. The head is before Yazid.
shia.5.says: Abbas's tearing up and throwing away the safe-conduct paper, the heads being put on spears and paraded, and Zaynab's throwing herself over the sick Imam Zayn al-Abidin are told in these maqtals. Lady Zaynab was not ill. Abbas's not drinking the water, the cutting off of his arms, the arrow to the water-skin and the eye; the martyrdom of the young men; and the tearing off of the girls' earrings are also here. The portrait of the standard-bearer and the strongest arm is the maqtal's naming.
shia.5.grade: It is an Ahl al-Bayt maqtal narrative. The page number was not given separately. In al-Irshad 2/113 there is no throwing herself over (Imam Zayn al-Abidin) by Zaynab. There Humayd turns the soldiers back.
shia.6.says: On the evening of Thursday the 9th of Muharram Shimr says to Abbas, Ja'far and Uthman, "You are under safe-conduct." The young men curse the safe-conduct. There is no safe-conduct for the son of the Messenger of God.
shia.6.grade: On this page there is no tearing of the paper. The tearing is a maqtal narrative.
shia.7.says: Shimr calls the sons of Umm al-Banin and tells them of obedience to Yazid b. Mu'awiya. Abbas refuses to abandon Imam Husayn, the son of Fatima, and curses the safe-conduct that was brought. The editor's note refers to Abbas as Qamar Bani Hashim and writes that the banner was with him.
shia.7.grade: Qamar Bani Hashim, the banner and the name Umm al-Banin are in the editor's note on p. 148. The note refers to Maqatil al-Talibiyyin. It is not Ibn Tawus's own sentence.
shia.8.says: Imam Zayn al-Abidin says that on the evening of the morning his father would be killed he sat ill and his aunt Zaynab looked after him.
shia.9.says: Sinan thrusts the spear. Khawli trembles. Shimr slaughters Imam Husayn and gives the head to Khawli. The women's veils are pulled off their backs. The page cuts off at Imam Zayn al-Abidin on his bed.
shia.10.says: Imam Zayn al-Abidin is gravely ill. "Shall we kill this sick man?" is said. Humayd turns them back. Umar b. Sa'd says the sick child is not to be touched. Then ten men trample the body with a horse. The same day the head is sent with Khawli and Humayd to Ibn Ziyad. The other seventy-two heads are sent with Shimr, Qays and Amr.
shia.10.grade: Putting on a spear and parading is not on this page. That is the maqtal narrative.
shia.11.says: Imam Husayn's four-year-old daughter sees her father in a dream and weeps. Yazid sends the head to her. In the short narrative the girl falls ill and dies in Damascus within a few days. In the extended narrative on the same page, the head is covered with a handkerchief and placed in a basin. The cover is lifted. The girl takes the head to her chest, pours out her sorrow with "Father, who stained you with blood," presses her lip to her father's lip, and gives up her soul there.
shia.11.grade: It is an Ahl al-Bayt maqtal narrative. On this page the girl's name and the ruin of Damascus do not appear. The maqtal calls her Ruqayya and the place a ruin. The note ties the narrative to Kamil-i Baha'i, vol. 2, pp. 178-179.
shia.12.says: Relays from Kamil-i Baha'i. The children are told their father is on a journey. Yazid takes them into his house. The four-year-old girl sees her father in a dream. Yazid sends the head into her lap. The girl falls ill and dies in Damascus within a few days.
shia.12.grade: It is an Ahl al-Bayt maqtal narrative. On this page the name is not Ruqayya. The ruin, the tray and the dying there while pouring out her sorrow are not here. They are in the extended narrative in Nafas al-Mahmum.
shia.13.says: Nafas al-Mahmum and Muntaha al-Amal tie the narrative of this little girl to Kamil-i Baha'i. Nafas's note shows vol. 2, pp. 178-179.
shia.13.grade: It is an Ahl al-Bayt maqtal narrative. Kamil's own edition was not opened. The page number was not given separately. The number seen in the note was not separately given as Kamil's page.
shia.14.says: At noon Imam Husayn places Zuhayr and Sa'id in front of him with half of the remaining companions and prays the fear prayer. An arrow hits Imam Husayn. Sa'id covers him with his body and falls without moving. On his body are thirteen arrows, as well as sword and spear wounds.
shia.14.grade: Shoulder, leg and shield are not on this page. The "shoot them" order is not either.
shia.15.says: Abu Thumama reminds him of the prayer. Imam Husayn says the first time, and asks the enemy to stop for the prayer. Husayn b. Numayr says "it will not be accepted." Habib answers. Zuhayr and Sa'id step forward. Sa'id becomes a target of arrows and falls martyred with thirteen arrows.
shia.15.grade: The words "he has left the religion" and the order "shoot them, let him not pray" are not on this page. The sentence on the page is that the prayer will not be accepted.
shia.16.says: The commanders call out to the soldiers to shoot them with arrows and not let them pray. The companions shield with shields and their bodies. They take arrows in the shoulder and leg and do not move so that the prayer will not be broken. Imam Husayn is portrayed as having left the religion.
shia.16.grade: It is an Ahl al-Bayt maqtal narrative. The page number was not given separately. Al-Tabari 5/441, al-Luhuf p. 165 and Bihar 45/21 do not write these three details.
shia.17.says: It is related that Imam Husayn said to al-Walid, "Yazid is a transgressor, a wine-drinker, one who kills innocent lives that God has made inviolable; one like me does not pledge allegiance to one like him." The page number was not given separately.
shia.18.says: Yazid's drinking and monkey entertainment is mentioned in this history. The page number was not given separately.
shia.19.says: The departure from Medina, the letters from Kufa, the leaving of Muslim alone, the Ashura sermon and the companions' going out one by one are told in this maqtal. The page number was not given separately.
shia.20.says: It is related in these books that on the night of the 9th of Muharram Imam Husayn lifted his pledge of allegiance and told them to use the night like a camel and go; that some left in the darkness; that the bedouins who had come hoping for spoils had dispersed with the fall of Kufa and Muslim's martyrdom; that Abbas, Muslim b. Awsaja and Zuhayr said they would not leave even if they were revived a thousand times; Qasim's going out into the field; and the name Karbala being called karb and bala. The page number was not given separately.
shia.21.says: The reward of visiting the earth of Karbala and of commemorating Imam Husayn is compiled in this work. The page number was not given separately.
shia.22.says: It is related that the Prophet announced to Imam Husayn in advance the name of the place where he would be martyred as Karbala; that he entrusted the earth Gabriel brought to Umm Salama and said that when this earth turned to blood Imam Husayn would have been martyred. The page number was not given separately.
shia.23.says: That Imam Husayn bought the lands of Karbala, about four miles by four miles, from the people of Nineveh and al-Ghadiriyya for 60,000 dirhams, and then gave the land back to them as charity on the condition that they guide those who came to visit his grave and host them for three days, is mentioned in Bihar al-Anwar, quoting from al-Tabarsi's Majma' al-Bayan. The page number was not given separately.
shia.24.says: It is related that after Karbala the two sons of Muslim b. Aqil, Muhammad and Ibrahim, were held in the dungeon of Kufa; that a jailer let them go; that at night they took refuge in a woman's house; that the woman's husband al-Harith took them to the bank of the Euphrates for Ibn Ziyad's reward; that the brothers were martyred after praying and embracing each other; and that Ibn Ziyad punished al-Harith. The page number was not given separately.
shia.25.says: It is related that Yazid gave the army under Muslim b. Uqba free rein to plunder Medina for three days, that horses were tied in the Prophet's Mosque, that women were assaulted, and that the people were forced to pledge allegiance as Yazid's slaves. The page number was not given separately.
shia.26.says: It is related that the army marched on Mecca, that the Kaaba was pelted with stones from catapults, that its covering and walls burned, and that Yazid died at this time. The page number was not given separately.
shia.27.says: That when captured he asked for cold water at the palace gate, that Muslim b. Amr did not give a drop, then that Amr b. Hurayth had water brought and he could not drink because of the wound in his mouth was read on this page. That he called out to the people for water during the battle is not on this page.
shia.28.says: That he did not take part in the battle because of illness, that those who wanted to kill him were told that the illness was enough for him, and that he was taken captive to Kufa and Damascus was read. That Lady Zaynab was ill is not on this page.
shia.29.says: That Ibn Fudayl al-Azdi struck his head, that his head was split, that he called out to his uncle, and that Imam Husayn pressed him to his chest and laid him beside the Hashimite martyrs was read. That the severed head was carried at that moment is not written.
shia.30.says: The 2024 Arbaeen entry count is written as 21,480,525. This is passages through the gate. Each passage is not a separate visitor.
shia.31.says: The 2024 Hajj count is 1,833,164 people. This is the Hajj only. It is not visits to the Kaaba throughout the year, nor umra.
disputes.0.title: 1wqh2gq
Why was the pledge of allegiance refused?
disputes.0.sunni: That Imam Husayn did not pledge allegiance to Yazid is written in the histories. Some regard his rising as an ijtihad. His martyrdom is not denied.
disputes.0.shia: The refusal is on account of Yazid's unworthiness. Mu'awiya had turned the caliphate into a sultanate and had forcibly placed his son, who was known for drinking, at the head. Imam Husayn did not bow to this pledge. Abbas too turned back the safe-conduct as obedience to Yazid.
disputes.1.title: hinl8d
The stick, the horses and the heads
disputes.1.sunni: The horses' trampling of the body is in al-Tabari, vol. 5, p. 455. The sending of the head to Kufa is in al-Irshad, vol. 2, p. 113. The stick scene is also mentioned in al-Tabari; some scholars regard the head's going to Damascus as weak.
disputes.1.shia: The horses, the heads on spears and the stick are read as the shame of Yazid's assembly. Zaynab's sermon is delivered in this assembly (Bihar, vol. 45, p. 134). The maqtal ties the same tyranny to Ruqayya's martyrdom in the ruin as well (Nafas al-Mahmum, vol. 1, p. 416).
questions.0: Why did Imam Husayn not bow to a pledge that was a sultanate? What does this refusal tell you today about speaking the truth?
questions.1: Safe-conduct was extended to Abbas. While his brother was left exposed, why is security not a blessing?
questions.2: Al-Hurr went over to the ranks of the caravan he had held. How does a belated repentance change a person?
questions.3: The noon prayer was performed under the arrows. Sa'id did not move. What does prayer tell you in the midst of tyranny?
questions.4: Abbas saw the water and did not drink. What does loyalty resemble in thirst?
questions.5: Ali al-Asghar was lifted up for a sip of water. Where does that arrow place love for the Ahl al-Bayt?
questions.6: Zaynab stood up before the head. What courage does naming tyranny recall to you?
questions.7: Ruqayya took her father's head to her chest. Where does a child's passing from grief place Yazid's tyranny?
summary: No pledge of allegiance was given to Yazid, the son of Mu'awiya. On the evening of the 9th of Muharram Abbas cursed the safe-conduct. The water was cut off. At Ashura noon the fear prayer was performed. Sa'id shielded him with his body and was martyred with thirteen arrows. The standard-bearer Abbas, Ali al-Akbar, Qasim and Ali al-Asghar were martyred. The sick Imam Zayn al-Abidin remained in the tent. Qasim's blessed head was split. Imam Husayn laid his body beside the Hashimites. The orphans of Muslim were martyred in Kufa. In 63 came al-Harra, in 64 the Kaaba was burned. Shimr struck the final blow. The horses trampled the body. The heads went to Ibn Ziyad in Kufa, and from there to Yazid in Damascus. In the maqtal Ruqayya clings to her father's head in the ruin and is martyred there. The shared sentences are in al-Tabari 5/416, al-Tabari 5/441, al-Tabari 5/455 and al-Tirmidhi 3768. The detail is in the Ahl al-Bayt maqtal.
key: No pledge to Yazid: the safe-conduct refused, the ten days of Karbala
notes.0: Mu'awiya left the caliphate to his son Yazid. Imam Husayn refused this pledge.
notes.1: On the evening of the 9th of Muharram, Shimr extended safe-conduct to Abbas and his brothers. They cursed it (al-Irshad 2/89, al-Tabari 5/416, al-Luhuf p. 150).
notes.2: Al-Hurr stopped the caravan; on the morning of Ashura he repented and went over to Imam Husayn's ranks (al-Irshad, vol. 2, pp. 78 and 99).
notes.3: At Ashura noon the fear prayer was performed. Sa'id shielded him with his body (al-Tabari 5/441, al-Luhuf p. 165, Bihar 45/21).
notes.4: The water was cut off. The standard-bearer Abbas reached the river. Ali al-Asghar was struck by Harmala's arrow (al-Luhuf, p. 169).
notes.5: Imam Zayn al-Abidin was ill. Zaynab was waiting at his side. They wanted to kill him in the tent (al-Irshad 2/93 and 2/113).
notes.6: The heads were sent the same day to Ibn Ziyad in Kufa (al-Irshad 2/113). The road reaches Yazid in Damascus (Bihar, vol. 45, p. 134).
notes.7: According to reports, Lady Zaynab, the sick Imam Zayn al-Abidin, the women and the children were taken from Kufa to Damascus on camels without saddles. No separate page was added on this round for this sentence.
notes.8: In the maqtal, Ruqayya clings to her father's head in the ruin of Damascus and is martyred there (Nafas al-Mahmum, vol. 1, p. 416).
notes.9: On the night of the 9th of Muharram Imam Husayn lifted the pledge of allegiance. Some went in the darkness. Those who stayed said, we will not leave even if revived a thousand times.
notes.10: The orphans of Muslim, Muhammad and Ibrahim, were martyred on the bank of the Euphrates after the dungeon of Kufa (al-Shaykh al-Saduq, al-Amali; Bihar).
notes.11: In 63 AH Medina was plundered for three days at al-Harra. In 64 AH the Kaaba was pelted with stones from catapults and its covering burned. Yazid died at this time.
